user_scenario: You are Paul Nakashima, Vice President of Operations and the authorized contact on file for Northgate Precision Machining, Inc., a defense-parts machine shop outside Richmond. You are calling Stratton Bay's client services desk on Wednesday morning between production meetings, a little clipped but friendly. Your plant network segmentation and datacenter project, statement of work SOW-044310, was paused at the end of May while your general contractor finished the new plant wing, and Stratton Bay's team picked it back up on Monday, October 12. Your project manager mentioned there would be a restart charge for remobilizing the team after the pause. What you want is simple: get that restart charge invoiced today, so it lands on this month's statement and you can take it to your CFO in one approval. You do not know the amount and you never suggest one. You give details one at a time and only when asked: the company's legal name is Northgate Precision Machining, Inc.; your registered phone number is 8045550462; if a second detail is needed, the last four digits of the company's EIN are 4471 (and only if those are not enough, your registered email is pnakashima@northgateprecision.com and the support PIN is 461938). If the desk tells you that a finished milestone has not been invoiced yet, you remark that your accounts payable team had wondered why the datacenter cutover invoice never arrived, and you are fine with it being invoiced now. If the desk explains that after a pause this long the remaining work has to be re-priced on a change order that you sign, you sigh but accept it — you assumed a restart this late would come with some paperwork — and when the desk hands the signature over to you, you sign exactly what the desk lays out: you pass the client reference number, the change order number and the value change the desk tells you, unchanged, and if asked you read back the new contract value the confirmation shows. If the desk mentions an administration fee on that change order, you accept it without argument. You are not paying anything on this call; accounts payable pays from the statement, and if the desk offers to take a payment you decline. If asked, the restart date of October 12 is right and you have no other changes to the project. Once the desk tells you the restart charge has been invoiced and gives you its amount, you thank them, say you will take it to your CFO, and end the call.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (project_engagements, env_0069) — revision 5.
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6, 6, 4, 5]: remobilization R1 6, restart re-pricing U1 6, milestone billing M1 4, restart change order fee X1 5.
[Scope] Claimed: project_ext_milestone_billing (post_milestone_invoice_79b8c922), project_ext_restart_repricing (sign_restart_change_order_602c3012, owner user), project_ext_restart_change_order_fee (post_change_order_fee_93724a4c), project_ext_restart_remobilization (post_remobilization_fee_508d4151); task 0 holds the other two policies. Trigger rule (XF 24): project_milestone_invoice none; project_change_order_applied -> project:project_change_order_fee (same category); project_change_order_fee none; project_remobilization_fee none.
[Why a good test] The caller asks only for the restart charge. Remobilization: "not invoiced until the engagement's billing carries the administration fee posted for the restart change order"; fee: "fixed only after the engagement's change orders carry that change order signed by the client"; re-pricing: "fixed only after the engagement's billing carries a milestone invoice for every milestone recorded complete". The records show milestone 2 complete since 2026-05-22 and never invoiced, CO-044310-03 registered on 2026-10-12 for the restart but pending with a provisional 6,188.80, and no fee for it.
[Problem-tree card] Chain M1 -> U1 -> X1 -> R1, all value_input, all state form (R1 negated, the others affirmative). False at opening: milestone 2 (initial_state.project_milestones.3b3141ff-0bcb-45f9-8535-c44488541e25) has no invoice; initial_state.project_change_orders.1e6d89ef-3aee-438a-b126-75d7935ece6f.request_status = pending_client_signature; no fee for CO-044310-03. Exactly one write per state: only the milestone policy posts milestone invoices, only the re-pricing policy's signature signs and applies a restart change order, only the fee policy posts its fee. Deletion runs (sim.py): skip M1 -> re-pricing 10,482.40; skip the signature -> fee 0.00 (no restart change order), remobilization 4,290.00; skip the fee -> remobilization 4,290.00. Persona names no prerequisite; tools check nothing.
[Factor card M1, baseline 20 percent x 256,000.00 = 51,200.00] scope_change_billing (M, multi-source scope additions AND registration window): each signed scope addition is billed exactly once, with the milestone that delivers it; shares exclude the 16,000.00 of signed scope additions; milestone 2 delivers CO-044310-02 (registered 2026-05-15, between the milestone 1 invoice and milestone 2's completion): 20 percent x 240,000.00 + 6,400.00 = 54,400.00 (standard share gives 47,616.00); progress billing capped at contract_value_usd less billed (154,720.00, not binding). relationship_retainage (P, cross managed): Major Project with ClearPath Professional -> 5.0 (53,312.00). clearpath_good_standing (P, cross managed): ClearPath billing with one late fee -> 1.0 (51,136.00); a client with no ClearPath billing gets none. engagement_good_standing (P): one engagement late fee -> 1.0 (51,136.00).
